FORM is a strong underfollowed HBM test/probe-card candidate; key survival tests are HBM revenue mix, customer breadth, margin profile, and durability into HBM4.
ONTO maps to the inspection/metrology subnode of AI advanced packaging and HBM expansion; verify backlog, HBM customer wins, and advanced packaging revenue materiality.
KLIC, TER, AEHR, COHU, ACLS, CAMT, and US-listed/ADR substrate or packaging-material names should be screened in a later pass, but evidence strength and AI revenue materiality vary.

The node is not only TSMC/ASML/HBM memory makers; second-order bottlenecks include OSAT capacity, HBM probe cards, inspection/metrology, thermocompression bonding, underfill/materials, ABF substrates, thermal interfaces, and test handlers.
AMKR should remain the US-listed OSAT reference anchor for advanced packaging/HBM integration, but later layers must test whether AI/HBM revenue is material versus broad packaging exposure.
FORM is a strong underfollowed candidate for HBM/advanced-packaging test because known-good-die and fine-pitch interposer verification are direct chokepoint-adjacent functions.
KLIC is a candidate for advanced-packaging equipment scarcity through thermocompression bonding, especially where AI, CPO, HPC, and heterogeneous integration overlap.

AEHR is a speculative-shadow candidate: direct AI processor test/burn-in orders exist, but survival through later layers depends on revenue materiality, customer concentration, and repeat-order durability.

This pass did not fully cover US-listed materials suppliers for underfill, thermal interface materials, ABF substrate exposure, or inspection/metrology beyond the selected names; these should be a follow-up Layer 1B subpass.
AMKR should be retained as the US-listed OSAT reference anchor for advanced packaging, but later layers must separate AI/HPC advanced-packaging economics from legacy mobile/consumer cyclicality.
FORM is a high-priority underfollowed test-gate candidate because HBM and advanced packaging increase probe-card and wafer-test intensity before expensive package integration.
KLIC is a mid-cap advanced-assembly equipment candidate whose HBM/FTC/vertical-wire evidence is improving, but repeat HBM orders and Advanced Solutions revenue mix need verification.
AEHR belongs in the speculative-shadow lane: AI processor burn-in evidence exists, but materiality, recurrence, and customer breadth must be proven before promotion.

This pass found stronger US-listed evidence in OSAT, probe cards, bonding, and burn-in/test than in ABF substrates, underfill, or thermal-interface materials; later passes should search non-US listings, ADRs, and suppliers embedded in electronics/materials conglomerates.
AMKR should remain the US-listed OSAT reference anchor for AI advanced-packaging capacity, but later layers must verify AI/HPC revenue materiality and customer commitments.

KLIC is a promising but more cyclical advanced-packaging equipment candidate; key evidence gap is whether HBM/TCB orders become recurring and material.
COHU maps to the HBM inspection and AI processor test subnode; later work should separate genuine AI/HBM system revenue from broader semiconductor cycle recovery.

node: Advanced packaging, HBM integration, leading-edge foundry, and semiconductor equipment
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe for the advanced packaging/HBM/foundry-capacity node with a two-lane structure: one reference anchor and three more direct underfollowed chokepoint suppliers. TSM is the obvious capacity anchor for leading-edge foundry and CoWoS-style packaging context. AMKR maps to outsourced advanced packaging/test capacity, FORM to HBM probe cards and semiconductor test intensity, ONTO to advanced packaging/HBM inspection and metrology. KLIC was a close alternate for thermocompression bonding, but was excluded to keep the list at four candidates. Expanded the US-listed universe around the advanced-packaging/HBM/test chokepoint with a two-lane list. AMKR is included as the reference OSAT anchor. FORM, KLIC, and AEHR are underfollowed or lower-attention equipment/test candidates tied to HBM known-good-die testing, thermocompression bonding for heterogeneous integration/co-packaged optics, and wafer/package-level burn-in for AI processors. This is a research universe only, not a trading recommendation. Later layers must verify AI revenue materiality, customer concentration, order durability, capacity constraints, and whether the market has already priced the bottleneck. Layer 1B expanded the US-listed universe for the advanced-packaging/HBM/test-capacity node. The pass deliberately avoided mega-cap GPU/foundry leaders except as context and surfaced four public assets with plausible direct or second-order exposure: one reference OSAT with unusually pure advanced-packaging exposure, two underfollowed mid-cap tool/test suppliers, and one smaller speculative test
